commits.pr_title: [Doc] Document /inference/v1/generate request/response fields and DP rank header
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`POST /inference/v1/generate` (token-in/token-out) has no field reference. A web search only surfaces the v0.20 pages, which show the old response format and no way to target a data-parallel rank. `docs/training/sampling_mask.md` also still says the endpoint returns logprob IDs as `token_id:<id>` strings; it now returns an integer `token_id`.

## Changes

- `docs/serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md`: how `--enable-scale-out` / `--tokens-only` register the endpoint (and the 403 otherwise), a curl example, request and response field tables, and the `X-data-parallel-rank` header. Existing sections and anchors (`#output-modes`, `#weight-versions`, `#aborting-requests`) are unchanged.
- `docs/training/sampling_mask.md`: `token_id:<id>` strings come from the OpenAI endpoints with `return_tokens_as_token_ids`; `/inference/v1/generate` returns an integer `token_id`.
- `examples/scale_out/token_generation_client.py`: docstring points to the page.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff, typos, markdownlint-cli2, mypy, SPDX, ...).
- `mkdocs build --strict` with `requirements/docs.txt` (as in `.readthedocs.yaml`, `fail_on_warning: true`): exit 0, no warnings. The page renders with the new anchors; `#weight-versions` (linked from `docs/training/async_rl.md`) and `#aborting-requests` still resolve.
- Facts checked against the code:
  - [`scale_out/factories.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/072c0886d53d933a7e1d3da7e8a3a91670cf181d/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L79-L95): `--tokens-only` always registers the endpoints; otherwise `--enable-scale-out` is required, else 403.
  - [`token_in_token_out/serving.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/072c0886d53d933a7e1d3da7e8a3a91670cf181d/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py#L214-L223): stop strings rejected on a `--tokens-only` server.
  - [`token_in_token_out/protocol.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/072c0886d53d933a7e1d3da7e8a3a91670cf181d/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py#L364-L374): logprob entries carry an integer `token_id`.
  - [`generate/base/serving.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/072c0886d53d933a7e1d3da7e8a3a91670cf181d/vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py#L219-L232): rank read from the `X-data-parallel-rank` header; non-integer values ignored.
  - [`v1/engine/input_processor.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/072c0886d53d933a7e1d3da7e8a3a91670cf181d/vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py#L396): ranks outside `[0, data_parallel_size)` rejected.
- Discoverability: before this change, an agent limited to web search could not answer how to call the endpoint and pin a DP rank. With this change, a fresh agent limited to the repo answered correctly with high confidence.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4] Overlap the unfused shared expert with AITER MegaMoE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` and an unfused shared expert, DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm ran the shared expert after the router and MegaMoE, on the main stream. This PR runs it on the aux stream next to the router + MegaMoE through `maybe_execute_in_parallel`. It follows the existing `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM` / `VLLM_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` convention: the overlap applies to steps of at most 256 tokens by default, and `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1` keeps the serial order. ATOM overlaps its shared expert with the routed experts the same way.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, AgentX agentic workload: P90 interactivity +2.7% at concurrency 128 and +6.4% at concurrency 64.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k.
- Prefill-sized steps and the fused shared-expert path are unchanged.

## Validation

Setup:
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8 AITER MegaMoE, shared expert unfused.
- AgentX agentic workload, 1200 s runs, requests counted in the 300-1200 s window.
- Single runs per configuration.

| | Without | With this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c128 (same node, same job): P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 27.13 | 27.87 (+2.7%) |
| c128: output tok/s/GPU | 335 | 346 (+3.3%) |
| c128: total tok/s/GPU | | +1.4% |
| c64 (same node, separate jobs): P90 interactivity | 48.26 | 51.33 (+6.4%) |
| c64: P50 interactivity | 61.65 | 64.31 (+4.3%) |
| c64: total tok/s/GPU | | -1.5% |
| gsm8k 5-shot, real speculative decoding (flexible / strict) | 0.9697 / 0.9704 | 0.9727 / 0.9735 |

Unit tests and lint:
- `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` on MI355X: 10 passed, against 6 on main. The 4 new cases run the shared expert on the aux stream.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, mypy included. This was rerun on the current main, which includes #61262.

## Details

- When MegaMoE fuses the shared expert, `shared_experts` is `None` and the routed path runs alone, as before.
- `maybe_execute_in_parallel` falls back to sequential execution when the stream is `None` and during breakable CUDA graph capture.
- #61262's runtime selection runs inside the MegaMoE call on the main stream, so it is not affected.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Build] Keep plain CUDA arch when its suffixed variant is also requested
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56548.

`cuda_archs_loose_intersection` silently drops a plain base arch (e.g. `10.0`) from
`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` when the list also contains its `a` suffixed variant (`10.0a`).
Introduced by #38126: the "Symmetric handling" block consumes SRC `10.0` for TGT `10.0a`,
so the plain TGT `10.0` finds nothing afterwards. Generic kernels (`_C`, `_moe_C`) then get
`sm_100a` only, which does not load on B300 (CC 10.3) and fails with
`cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice`.

Changes in `cmake/utils.cmake`:

- Symmetric-suffix block: only remove the SRC base arch when TGT does not also request the
  plain base. Both `10.0` and `10.0a` are then emitted, matching torch's handling of the
  same list.
- Exact-base loop: after a suffixed SRC entry (e.g. `10.0f`) matched a plain TGT base, also
  drop TGT's own `a`/`f` variants of that base so the family fallback does not add a second
  cubin (`10.0a` next to `10.0f`) for the same source.

## Test Plan

Ran the function directly with `cmake -P` (no GPU needed), before and after, with
`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5 8.0 8.6 8.7 8.9 9.0a 10.0 10.0a 12.0 12.1+PTX"` on CUDA 13
(`CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS="7.5;8.0;8.6;8.7;8.9;9.0;10.0;11.0;12.0"`), plus the per-kernel
lists used in `CMakeLists.txt`. Regression inputs: `10.0a`, `10.0`, `9.0a;10.0f;12.0f`,
`8.0;9.0;10.0;12.0`, `7.5;8.0;8.9;9.0a;12.0`.

## Test Result

| list | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| global `CUDA_ARCHS` | `9.0a;10.0a;7.5;8.0;8.6;8.7;8.9;12.0` | `9.0a;10.0a;7.5;8.0;8.6;8.7;8.9;10.0;12.0` |
| `9.0a;10.0f;10.1f;10.3f;12.0f;12.1f` (cutlass w8a8) | `12.0f;9.0a;10.0a` | `10.0f;12.0f;9.0a` |
| `10.0f` (scaled_mm SM100) | `10.0a` | `10.0f` |
| `8.0;8.6;8.9;9.0a;10.0f;12.0f` | `12.0f;9.0a;10.0a;8.0;8.6;8.9` | `10.0f;12.0f;9.0a;8.0;8.6;8.9` |

All five regression inputs produce identical output before and after. The "after" global list
is what v0.18.x produced for this input (`10.0` present), and the per-kernel lists go back to
the family targets that `CMakeLists.txt` documents as the intended CUDA >= 12.9 path.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Build DeepEP for SM103 (B300/GB300) in the Docker image
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Docker image builds DeepEP for `9.0a 10.0a` only, so DeepEP cannot run on SM103 (B300/GB300). This adds `10.3a` to DeepEP's arch list when building with CUDA >= 12.9.

## Claims

- `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput` (and the other DeepEP backends) work on SM103 GPUs with the image's DeepEP.
- No change for CUDA < 12.9 builds (12.8 has no SM103 target) or for other GPUs: `9.0a` and `10.0a` cubins are unchanged.

## Validation

On 8x B300 (SM103, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, NVSHMEM 3.4.5), DeepEP at the image's commit (`d4f41e4e`) built with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='10.0a 10.3a'`, replacing the DeepEP wheel in `vllm/vllm-openai` v0.31.0:

| Check | Stock image DeepEP (`9.0a 10.0a`) | With `10.3a` |
|---|---|---|
| `cuobjdump --list-elf deep_ep/_C*.so` | `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` | `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` |
| `tests/legacy/test_intranode.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 4096 --hidden 6144 --num-topk 8 --num-experts 256` | n/a (kernels cannot launch) | 24/24 dispatch/combine checks pass (BF16/FP8, sync/async); best dispatch FP8 0.41 ms, combine 0.67 ms |
| `vllm serve` GLM-5.3 FP8, prefill context parallel 8 + EP 8, `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput` | startup fails: `CUDA runtime exception (DeepEP/csrc/kernels/legacy/intranode.cu:21): 999 (cudaErrorUnknown)` | starts with `DeepEPHTAll2AllManager`; greedy answers match the default all2all backend on a fixed prompt set |

Version gating of the shell snippet (`CUDA_VERSION` from the stage):

```
CUDA 12.8.1 -> 9.0a 10.0a
CUDA 12.9.1 -> 9.0a 10.0a 10.3a
CUDA 13.0.3 -> 9.0a 10.0a 10.3a
```

Not done: a full rebuild of this Dockerfile (the change only alters the DeepEP arch list passed to `install_python_libraries.sh`). CI has no SM103 runners, so this path is not exercised in CI. `pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile` passes (with `update-dockerfile-graph` skipped locally: the stage graph is unchanged).

## Details

- Root cause: arch-specific (`a`) cubins only run on their exact compute capability, and DeepEP's build embeds no PTX, so `sm_100a` code does not load on SM103 (10.3). The failure surfaces as `cudaErrorUnknown` (999) from DeepEP's legacy intranode/layout kernels at the first dispatch.
- `10.3a` requires CUDA 12.9+, hence the gate on `CUDA_VERSION`; the default image is CUDA 13.0.
- Build time grows by one more arch for DeepEP only (its wheel is built in parallel with the csrc build).
- Performance is not a claim of this PR. On the configuration above, a closed-loop real-prompt prefill load (12 and 24 requests in flight, unique prompt prefixes, `cached_tokens` = 0) measured, in prompt tokens/s: `allgather_reducescatter` with FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE 60.4k / 60.7k, `deepep_high_throughput` (which selects DeepGEMM MoE) 56.5k / 56.9k, `deepep_v2` with FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE 54.0k / 62.2k (the first run includes DeepEP v2 JIT warm-up). Single runs on one node. An earlier version of this description cited a DeepEP gain; that comparison was inflated by prefix-cache hits from repeated prompts and is withdrawn.

commits.pr_title: [Qwen4Exp] Clean up HC and PLE implementations for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Clean up Qwen4Exp HC/PLE implementations and refine PLE quantization selection, with regression coverage for the affected paths.

## Claims

- **Remove redundant custom-op registrations,** dispatcher wrappers, and fake implementations for NVIDIA HC operations and the shared PLE gate. Call the existing Triton kernel launch functions directly.
- **Move checkpoint shard overlap and copy helpers** into `PLEVocabParallelEmbedding`, using the embedding's own TP shard metadata.
- **Rename HC** `lora_rank` to `hc_lowrank` and local `lora` **variables** to `lowrank` on NVIDIA and AMD. **Use clearer names** for token counts and tensor dimensions in HC and PLE launch functions.
- **Reuse `round_up`** for PLE vocabulary padding, QSA RoPE-position alignment, QSA ring capacity, and prefill logits alignment.
- **Refine PLE quantization selection**: honor ModelOpt layer exclusions, retain serialized FP8 support, **warn and fall back to unquantized PLE for unsupported global configurations**, and reject unsupported explicit ModelOpt per-layer algorithms, embedding dtype overrides, and nonserialized `Fp8Config` usage.

## Validation

**Correctness tests:**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py -q
```

Result: **123 passed, 2 skipped**. The skipped cases require ROCm. Coverage includes HC and PLE kernel correctness, checkpoint shard loading, FP8 handling, pinned-host lookup and prefetch, and quantization selection.

**Static checks:** Ruff lint and formatting checks passed for all 12 changed files. `git diff --check` also passed.

**Serving smoke validation:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next started and served HTTP 200 requests with BF16, TP2/DP1, CPU-offloaded PLE, and MTP with 3 speculative tokens. The run recorded nonzero MTP acceptance.

**CI coverage:** Existing CPU CI covers PLE quantization selection and shard-loading tests. The H200 job covers HC operations and PLE convolution correctness.

End-to-end model accuracy evaluations and before/after performance benchmarks were not run. ROCm hardware execution and quantized-checkpoint serving validation remain pending.

## Details

The unquantized PLE fallback assumes the checkpoint contains an unquantized embedding table. NVFP4 PLE decoding and format conversion remain outside this change.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Score with the chat template declared by Sentence Transformers CrossEncoders
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Score Sentence Transformers (v5.4+) CrossEncoders with the chat template they declare, so they work without `--chat-template`. 

This closes #60409, follow-up to #31563, and is complementary to #55359 (see Details).

## Claims

- A CrossEncoder whose single `sequence-classification` Transformer module declares the `message` modality in `sentence_bert_config.json` is now scored like in Sentence Transformers: `query`/`document` messages rendered with the saved chat template (the default one, or the named template from `processing_kwargs.chat_template.chat_template`).
- The other `processing_kwargs.chat_template` settings (e.g. `add_generation_prompt`) are passed to the template, like in Sentence Transformers; request `chat_template_kwargs` override them.
- `--chat-template` (or `LLM.score(chat_template=...)`) still takes precedence, and an invalid Sentence Transformers config then doesn't block startup. Checkpoints without this metadata, and models with a built-in score template (`SupportsScoreTemplate`), are unchanged.
- The template is resolved once at startup and logged. A declared template that the checkpoint doesn't have (including an unknown name) fails at startup, instead of silently falling back to pair encoding or to vLLM's fallback templates.

## Validation

- MTEB (NFCorpus, RTX 4080 SUPER): `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` without `--chat-template` scores 0.33922 (bf16) vs 0.33919 for Sentence Transformers 5.7.0 (fp32). Without this change: 0.30173, the test fails.
  `pytest tests/models/language/pooling_mteb_test/test_nemotron.py -k rerank`
- Online, with a tiny random Qwen3 CrossEncoder saved in the Sentence Transformers format: `vllm serve <tiny checkpoint> --runner pooling`, then `/rerank` and `/score` return the same scores as Sentence Transformers (0.51295, 0.519637), and `chat_template_kwargs: {"add_generation_prompt": false}` overrides the saved setting.
- Unit tests: `pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py -k sentence_transformers tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py`
- `pre-commit run` passes.
- Real-world checkpoint with this layout: `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` (its `chat_template.jinja` was synced with vLLM in its commit "Share reranking chat template across Sentence Transformers and vLLM"). `test_reranker` in `tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py` now runs without `chat_template` and still matches the HF reference on text and image documents (RTX 4080 SUPER, fp16). Without this change it fails (first text pair: HF 0.3191, vLLM 0.0575).
  `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py -k test_reranker`
- On that model, the automatic path produces the same token IDs (BOS included) and scores as `--chat-template examples/pooling/score/template/nemotron-vl-rerank.jinja`.

## Details

- Detection is limited to the exact layout Sentence Transformers uses for sequence-classification CrossEncoders (`model_type: CrossEncoder`, one Transformer module at the root, `transformer_task: sequence-classification`, `message` in `modality_config`). Many rerankers inherit an unrelated chat template from their base LLM, so the tokenizer template is still never used without this explicit declaration, as discussed in #31563.
- The nemotron-rerank-vl reranker test and docs no longer pass `--chat-template` (separate commit).
- Message contents are passed as strings, like with `--chat-template`, so multimodal placeholders keep working.
- The templated prompt is tokenized as with `--chat-template` (default `add_special_tokens`). Plain transformers tokenizers render Sentence Transformers prompts with `add_special_tokens=False`, but custom processors may not: `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2`'s processor tokenizes its prompts with the default and adds BOS. Keeping vLLM's existing behavior matches the only checkpoint with this layout I found (verified above); for Qwen3-based rerankers (no BOS) both are identical.
- `restore_suffix` (restoring the template suffix after truncation) is not implemented; the startup log and the docs say to use `max_tokens_per_doc` to truncate documents.
- The config is read in `CrossEncoderIOProcessor` rather than `ModelConfig`, since only scoring uses it and this avoids touching `ModelConfig` and its hash. If #55359 lands first, this can move next to its `sentence_transformers_config`.
- `LLM(chat_template=...)` is still not used by `LLM.score` (unchanged); the saved template applies there, and `LLM.score(chat_template=...)` overrides it.
- Relation to #55359: it handles the modular `Transformer -> Pooling -> Dense` and `Transformer -> LogitScore` layouts and leaves single-module checkpoints unchanged, so the two PRs do not overlap functionally. I kept the same module-type constant and setting names so they can be merged in either order; whichever lands second can reuse the other's helpers (e.g. its `restore_suffix` implementation).
- `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` revisions between its Sentence Transformers integration (April 2026) and b8a9987 (October 2026) declare the `message` modality but only ship the Llama 3 chat template inherited from the base model. Without `--chat-template`, those revisions were already scored without the right prompt; they still need the flag, as the docs now say.
- Motivation: `polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm` (zerank-2 converted to `Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`, template added in #60415) can declare its score template this way instead of requiring `--chat-template`.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Per-test timeout for Language Models (Extended Pooling)
commits.pr_body:
Shard 3/4 of `language-models-test-extended-pooling` has hung on every full CI run since Oct 16 (builds 95480, 95553, 95634). Shards 1, 2 and 4 take 12-21 minutes; shard 3/4 stalls in `test_colbert.py::TestColbertSharedEngine::test_colbert_token_embed[bert]` right after the `test_bge_m3` API-server tests, and Buildkite cancels it at the 150-minute limit.

A cancelled job also keeps the full run's coverage collect steps from running (`allow_dependency_failure` doesn't cover a cancelled dependency), so the ci-selector's recordings haven't been published since Oct 15.

This adds `--timeout=900 --timeout-method=thread` (`pytest-timeout` is already in `requirements/test/cuda.txt`). A hung test now fails with a stack dump, so whoever owns the ColBERT test gets a trace of where it hangs, and the job ends as failed rather than cancelled. It doesn't fix the hang itself.

commits.pr_title: [Doc][RL] Document the weight-transfer HTTP protocol for trainers without vLLM
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Documents the HTTP wire protocol for the `nccl` and `ipc` weight-transfer backends, for a trainer that does **not** import vLLM. The contract goes into the existing NCCL and IPC engine pages, and the PR adds two minimal reference trainers. Until now the contract was only described by the code in `nccl_common.py`, `ipc_engine.py`, `packed_tensor.py`, and `clients.py`.

## Claims

- `docs/training/weight_transfer/nccl.md`: new section **"Trainer Without vLLM over HTTP"** covering:
  - `init_info` fields, including `nccl_unique_id_b64`
  - the worker rank formula
  - the one-element fp32 warm-up `all_reduce`
  - `update_info` (`names` / `dtype_names` / `shapes`)
  - broadcast order, which runs concurrently with `/update_weights`
  - packed chunking: a chunk closes *after* it overflows
  - torch-only communicator options, with the caveat that reading store key `"0"` relies on torch internals
  - init has no timeout
- `docs/training/weight_transfer/ipc.md`: same section for IPC, covering:
  - the `ipc_handles_pickled` format
  - the GPU UUID key, which has no `GPU-` prefix
  - `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1` on the server
  - `tensor_sizes`
  - packed chunking: a chunk closes *before* it overflows
  - keeping tensors alive until finish, then `ipc_collect`
  - multi-rank handle gathering to rank 0
- `docs/training/weight_transfer/README.md`:
  - the endpoint table gains the missing `/shutdown_weight_transfer_engine` row
  - a short paragraph says a trainer may implement the protocol directly and links both sections. The motivation: the trainer stays decoupled from vLLM, with no vLLM install or version pin, so trainer and server can upgrade independently, and non-PyTorch trainers such as JAX can use it
  - the shared failed-update caveat is stated once
- `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py` and `examples/rl/rlhf_http_ipc_no_vllm.py`:
  - import only `torch`, `requests`, `safetensors`, `pybase64` and the stdlib
  - a `sys.meta_path` blocker makes any `vllm` import fail
  - print generations before and after the sync
- `tools/pre_commit/check_forbidden_imports.py`: one-line `pickle` allowlist entry for the IPC example, because pickle is the only HTTP encoding for IPC handles.

## Validation

Ran the example trainers from this branch on GB200 (aarch64) with image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-aarch64-dev-20261016-49cb2bb`. That image is within a few commits of `main`, with no differences in the dense nccl/ipc paths or the routes. Model: Qwen3-0.6B.

Each server started with `--load-format dummy`. After each sync, `/weight_checker compare` checked the weights against checksums from a server cold-loaded with the same checkpoint at the same TP. `/weight_checker reset` zeroed the weights between runs.

| Backend | Server | Trainer | Mode | `/weight_checker compare` | Generation after sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| nccl | TP=2 (GPUs 0-1) | GPU 2 | unpacked | match, 0/452 mismatches | " Paris. The capital of France is also the capital of the Republic of France." |
| nccl | TP=2 | GPU 2 | packed (64 MiB) | match, 0/452 | same |
| ipc | TP=1 (GPU 0) | GPU 0 | unpacked | match, 0/226 | same |
| ipc | TP=1 | GPU 0 | packed (512 MiB) | match, 0/226 | same |
| ipc | TP=2 (GPUs 0-1) | GPUs 0-1, `--num-gpus 2` | unpacked | match, 0/452 | same |
| ipc | TP=2 | GPUs 0-1 | packed | match, 0/452 | same |

- Every trainer exited 0, and `vllm` never appeared in its loaded modules.
- Before each sync, generation was gibberish (dummy weights) or `!!!!` (zeroed weights).
- The NCCL runs also exercise `/shutdown_weight_transfer_engine`, then re-init on a fresh unique id.
- The documented fields were checked against current `main` source.
- The torch-communicator table and the failed-update caveat come from an earlier verification on `ac9126e58`:
  - `torch.cuda.nccl.init_rank` fails with `PY_SSIZE_T_CLEAN`
  - ctypes against torch's bundled `libnccl` works
  - a failed `/update_weights` leaves the model mid-reload
- Since that GPU run, the examples changed only in docstrings, so they were not re-run.

Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, typos, markdownlint, mypy, forbidden-imports, torch-cuda check, sign-off). `mkdocs build` succeeds, and both `#trainer-without-vllm-over-http` anchors are generated.

Repro (the server command lines are in each example's docstring):
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py --url http://localhost:8000 --checkpoint /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B [--packed]
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python examples/rl/rlhf_http_ipc_no_vllm.py --url http://localhost:8000 --checkpoint /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B --num-gpus 2 [--packed]
```

## Details

- **No duplicate:** `gh pr list --search` for "weight transfer http", "nccl_unique_id_b64", "JAX trainer", and "[Doc] weight transfer" finds no open PR documenting this contract.
- **#57854** (failed-update handling) may change the README caveat. If it merges first, that line should be updated.
- **No server spawn:** the examples assume an already running server instead of starting `vllm serve`, because a trainer without vLLM usually runs in a different environment from the server.
- **Torch internal:** the NCCL example gets the unique id from `ProcessGroupNCCL.eager_connect_single_device` through store key `"0"`. The doc and the example both label this as a torch implementation detail, and the ctypes route is listed as an alternative.
- **Not in Buildkite:** the examples need a separately launched server and a local checkpoint. The existing `rlhf_http_{nccl,ipc}.py` CI steps already exercise the same server-side paths.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Release] Fix release wheel builds: stop excluding tracked recipes/ from Docker context
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the release pipeline, broken since #61302 ([release-v2 #8603](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/8603)). The CUDA x86_64/aarch64 and ROCm wheel builds fail, which breaks every downstream image and publish step:

```
#58 0.576 Repo is dirty
ERROR: failed to solve: process "/bin/sh -c if [ \"$GIT_REPO_CHECK\" != \"0\" ]; then bash tools/check_repo.sh ; fi" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

**Root cause:** #61302 added `/recipes` to `.dockerignore`. Those 188 files are tracked, and `.git` is bind-mounted into the build, so git sees them as deleted. Two things then break:
- `tools/check_repo.sh` (`git diff --quiet`) fails release builds, which set `GIT_REPO_CHECK=1`.
- setuptools-scm stamps the wheel `...+g<sha>.dYYYYMMDD`, while the Rust frontend build pins `dirty=false`. This fails `test_show_version` in the H200 Rust Frontend OpenAI/Serve-Admin Coverage steps on main.

**Fix:** drop `/recipes` from `.dockerignore`. It's about 1.5 MB of YAML in the build context and isn't installed into the image. A new test, `test_dockerignore_keeps_tracked_root_paths`, fails if a root-anchored `.dockerignore` entry ever excludes tracked files again.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches `.dockerignore`. This supersedes #62214, which only masked the version symptom and would not fix `check_repo.sh`.

## Test Plan

- I extracted the new test's logic and ran it standalone (the repo conftest needs a full env): 188 tracked files excluded on `origin/main`, 0 on this branch.
- Release and Docker builds were not run locally; the release pipeline will confirm.

## Overview

`FUSED_GDN_DECODE_ARCHS` is set only inside the `CUDA >= 13.0` block of `CMakeLists.txt`. This PR builds the kernel for `8.0;8.6;8.9;9.0a` when CUDA < 13.0. The family targets (`10.0f;11.0f;12.0f`) still need CUDA 13.

Builds on #51674 (kernel, "only needs cp.async and BF16 math"), #52743 (Ampere declaration guard) and #53835 (SM110 target).

- CUDA 12.9 builds include the fused GDN MTP decode kernel for SM80–SM90.
- No change for CUDA ≥ 13.0 builds.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix speculative warmup deadlock with pipeline parallelism
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix a pipeline-parallel startup deadlock in MRV2 speculative decoding introduced by [#59260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59260).

## Claims

- Ensure all PP stages participate in the additional greedy warmup pass.
- Add regression coverage for matching warmup rounds across PP stages, with speculative decoding enabled and disabled.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py -q
```

- **34 passed** in 9.64 seconds. These suites are covered by the existing `V1 Executor + Worker` CI job.
- **GLM-4.7-Flash smoke test passed**: MRV2, TP=2, PP=2, BF16, MTP with one speculative token, JIT warmup and CUDA graphs enabled.
- Warmup completed and generation produced exactly **1,024 tokens** using `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, and `ignore_eos=True`. Recorded 532 draft tokens and 492 accepted tokens; process exited successfully.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

The model run validates startup and generation; no accuracy benchmark was performed.

## Details

Only the last PP stage owns a rejection sampler. Previously, the additional greedy warmup pass was gated on its presence, so earlier stages skipped the pass while the last stage waited for their activations.

Gate this pass on `speculative_config` instead, ensuring every PP stage executes matching forwards. The change is limited to the warmup condition and regression tests.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Give the MoE parallel-launch watchdog room for AITER JIT builds
commits.pr_body:
Raises the parallel-launch watchdog added in #61695 from 900 s to 1800 s on ROCm only, so `MoE Kernels Shard 1` on AMD CI stops timing out while AITER JIT-compiles its CK MoE modules. Related: ROCm/aiter#5766.

- Fixes `test_modular_kernel_combinations_singlegpu[...AiterFp8TensorExperts-1]` on MI300, which can never finish within 900 s.
- No change on CUDA or other platforms (still 900 s, which is what #61695 needs for the B200 NVSHMEM hang).

AITER JIT build times for the stage modules this case needs, from the logs above (MI300, gfx942):

| Module | main #14821 | #14868 |
|---|---|---|
| `module_moe_ck2stages_f8_f8_preshuffle_off_b16_silu_per_tensor_mulWeightStage1` | 595 s | — (killed) |

- **Not yet validated on hardware:** the case needs gfx942/gfx950 and I only have MI250 locally. This PR stays a draft until AMD CI's `MoE Kernels Shard 1` passes on it.

Root cause: the AITER wheel built in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` (`PREBUILD_KERNELS=1`) ships only the `preshuffle_on` fp8 `moe_ck2stages` modules. `AiterFp8TensorExperts` uses the `preshuffle_off` ones, so the first launch compiles two modules (~10 min each) inside the watched region. The real fix is on the AITER side (prebuild these modules, see ROCm/aiter#5766); then this bump can be reverted.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Wait for pending expert buffer copies before NIXL READs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes the intermittent `test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy[nixl-*]` failure in `mi300_4: (MI300) EPLB Execution`:

```text
verify_redundant_experts_have_same_weights failed: rank=0, layer=0, weight_idx=0, logical_expert=1, physical_pos=4, actual_head=[2100.0, 2101.0, ...], reference_head=[1000.0, 1001.0, ...]
FAILED distributed/test_eplb_execute.py::test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy[nixl-4-2-2-5] - AssertionError
```

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14810/list?jid=01a143f1-ca27-459c-90a8-b3ef97f5fcaf&tab=output>

The test encodes weights as `logical_expert * 1000 + layer * 100 + ...`, so layer 0 ends up with experts from layer 1. `move_from_buffer` only queues the copies out of `expert_buffer` on the stream, and `add_recv` for the next layer immediately issues NIXL READs into the same buffer from the CPU. The READs are not ordered with the stream, so when the GPU lags (e.g. waking up from idle), they overwrite the buffer before the copies of the previous layer run. Only multi-layer cases fail.

The original NIXL communicator (#36276) synchronized the stream before issuing READs. #41633 removed that sync together with the send buffer packing and made `set_stream` a no-op, while READs now land directly in `expert_buffer`. 

This PR synchronizes the current stream and the EPLB stream in `set_transfer_context`, before the first READ of each layer, and removes the no-op `set_stream` override so the stream is stored. The current stream covers the sync path. In async EPLB, the main thread copies out of the buffer on the main stream, which the worker sees only through `self._stream` waiting on `consumed_event`.

## Test Plan

MI300X (gfx942):

```bash
cd tests
pytest -v -s distributed/test_eplb_execute.py
```

To trigger the race, I ran the `nixl-4-2-2-5` and `nixl-2-2-3-4` cases of `test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy` in a loop with the same seed and expert mapping as CI, either with the GPU idle for 2 s before each rearrangement or with a `torch.cuda._sleep` delay before `move_from_buffer`.

## Test Result

| Setup | `main` | `main` + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPU idle 2 s before each rearrangement | 5/100 failed | 0/100 failed |
| 10-20 ms GPU delay before `move_from_buffer` | 20/20 failed | 0/10 failed |
| Async EPLB flow, 10 ms GPU delay | 40/40 failed | 0/40 failed |

The async flow was emulated with a worker thread calling `transfer_layer` and the main thread calling `move_from_buffer`, as in `async_worker.py` and `eplb_state.py`. All failures had the same signature as CI, while `torch_gloo`, `pynccl` and `torch_nccl` passed under the same delay.

With this PR, `distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` passes: `35 passed, 7 skipped`.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation and validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [NIXL] Drop unreachable producer-side notif counting in push mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove the producer-side branch of `NixlPushConnectorWorker._get_new_notifs`, which no push-mode code path can reach. Split out of #61488 / #61580 as an independent simplification, as suggested in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61580#issuecomment-6237375565.

## Claims

- No behavior change for P or D in push mode: the removed branch only ran on a plain `"<req_id>:<n>"` notif arriving at P, which push mode never sends.
- `_get_new_notifs` now only counts consumer-side completion notifs and always returns an empty set; P keeps reporting finished sends from its WRITE handles in `get_transfer_results`.
- 26 insertions, 59 deletions.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py`: 103 passed.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`: 182 passed. The two `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller` cases fail locally on main as well.
- With a tripwire in the removed branch, the push, heartbeat and NIXL connector unit tests pass without reaching it.
- On GB200, the tripwire was not reached in end-to-end push runs with TP1 → TP1, producer TP2 → consumer TP1 and producer TP1 → consumer TP2, and those runs met their expected outputs. These runs used the same `push_worker.py` change on the #61488 branch.

## Details

In push mode, D sends P only two kinds of notifs:
- `PUSH_REG`, consumed by the writer thread before notifs are forwarded to `_get_new_notifs`;
- `HB:`, handled at the top of `_get_new_notifs` before the counting.

Plain `"<req_id>:<n>"` notifs to P come from `_pending_recv_notifs`, which only `pull_worker.py` fills. P → D completion notifs are attached to the push WRITEs and are counted on D, which is the branch this PR keeps.

The removed code is the producer-side counting copied from pull mode, the `transfer_topo` assert it needed, and the counter cleanup for finished pushes in `get_transfer_results`. commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes the macOS arm64 CPU wheel build, which fails on main (release-v2 #8588) and on `releases/v0.32.0` (release-v2 #8575):

```
error[E0599]: no method named `domain` found for struct `socket2::Socket` in the current scope
 --> src/engine-core-client/src/transport.rs:408:25
408 |     let domain = socket.domain()?;
```

#54113 uses `socket2::Socket::domain()` (`SO_DOMAIN`) in `adopt_listener` to tell inherited TCP and Unix listeners apart. socket2 only provides that method on Linux, Android, FreeBSD and Fuchsia, so `vllm-rs` doesn't compile on macOS. The macOS wheel is in the "additional wheels" group, which only runs when unblocked, so nothing caught this when it landed.

## Change

Read the family from the listener's bound address instead: `socket.local_addr()?.domain()`. `SockAddr::domain` works on every platform. The TCP/Unix branching after it is unchanged.

Also adds `inherited_unix_listener_is_adopted_without_rebinding`, a Unix-socket counterpart to the existing inherited TCP listener test. Before this, the Unix branch had no test.

## Test Plan

On macOS (arm64, rustc 1.95):
- `cargo check -p vllm-engine-core-client`: failed with the error above before the change, passes after.
- `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client inherited`: both inherited listener tests pass (TCP and Unix).
- `cargo check --manifest-path rust/src/cmd/Cargo.toml --release --features native-tls-vendored --bin vllm-rs`, the wheel build's cargo invocation: passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.

Linux CI covers the Linux path.

Wanted for v0.32.0 (milestone "v0.32.0 cherry picks"), since it blocks the macOS wheel there too.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Enable inductor batch-invariant mode under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With torch.compile (used under batch invariance for quantized models, among others), RMSNorm and the other vLLM custom ops are lowered by inductor instead of using vLLM's batch-invariant kernels. Inductor picks the tile config of its reduction kernels in each worker process by on-device autotuning among candidates whose reduction block differs (`dynamic_scale_rblock`), and the reduction block sets the fp32 accumulation order: logging the decisions (`TORCH_LOGS=+torch._inductor.runtime.triton_heuristics`, block 3c) shows the same fused residual-add + RMSNorm kernel autotuned to `R0_BLOCK: 1024` in some workers and compiled pieces and to `R0_BLOCK: 512` in others, so two workers can norm the same row to different bits. Inductor has a batch-invariant mode for exactly this (`torch._inductor.config.batch_invariant`, "stable per-sample compiled kernel across batch sizes"; it implies inductor's deterministic mode, which skips that autotuning), but `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` did not enable it: every generated kernel carried `'deterministic': False, 'batch_invariant': False` in its `inductor_meta`.

This showed up as MoE models served with DP > 1, TP > 1 and expert parallelism not being batch invariant. The split itself is not specific to that layout: the DP=4 x TP=1 + EP layout's fused norm kernel shows it too (block 3c), and that layout passed the check in every run here. What the sequence-parallel MoE path adds is that a token's MoE input is the post-attention norm output of whichever TP rank's chunk holds the token, and that depends on the token's position in the batch, so within one replica the disagreement becomes a batch dependence. The failure is intermittent (1 to 14 of 32 prompts per run, usually a sampled token flipping at a late decode step from a small logprob change), and it disappears with `--enforce-eager`, with the custom ops kept (`custom_ops=all` or `none,+rms_norm`), with dynamo alone (`DYNAMO_TRACE_ONCE`), or with `TORCHINDUCTOR_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` / `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1`; it stays with CUDA graphs off, with every fusion pass off, with the EP combine replaced by an all-to-all + fixed-order sum, with the router padding mask chunk-aligned, and with `moe_forward`'s stale `mutates_args` removed.

This PR sets inductor's `batch_invariant` config in `enable_batch_invariant_mode()`, which every worker runs before compiling. Nothing changes when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is unset. With it, the DP x TP + EP deployment passes with sequence-parallel MoE enabled.

The first revision of this PR disabled sequence-parallel MoE under batch invariance as a stopgap; following review, it now fixes the cause instead, and the evidence below replaces the earlier description.

## Test Plan

Online bitwise check (32 prompts, `temperature=0.6`, fixed seed, `max_tokens=8`, each prompt alone vs all 32 in one batched request, per-step top logprobs compared bitwise; "ragged" uses 1024-2048-word prompts), server started with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, 4x GB300 (SM103), `main` at `c19c263ac8`, torch 2.13.0:

- `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4` (VLLM_CUTLASS NvFp4 MoE experts), DP=2 x TP=2 + EP: `main` (several server starts, the failure is intermittent), `main` + `TORCHINDUCTOR_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (the env form of what the patch sets), `main` + this PR (one run with `TORCH_COMPILE_DEBUG=1` to show the generated kernels' `inductor_meta`).
- Regressions: TP=4 (env form and this PR), DP=4 x TP=1 + EP (env form).
- `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` (Triton WNA16 MoE experts, on a tree that also carries the pending #61038 fix for that path): `main`, env form, this PR.
- Cost: `vllm bench serve` (random 1024/128 x256 and 64/256 x128 prompts, 16 warmups, seed 0), `main` vs this PR, DP=2 x TP=2 + EP (one run each) and TP=4 (two runs each).
- Regression: the batch-invariance test suite (22 ids of `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py`), `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4` TP=1, `main` and this PR side by side.
- A table of every other configuration tried during the bisection (one server start each).

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Parser] Stream Qwen3 tool argument values incrementally (12 KB call: 2.1 s to 11 ms)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Streaming a Qwen3 XML tool call re-parses the whole argument on every delta: `_qwen3_arg_converter`, then `_safe_arg_prefix`, a per-character Python loop over the full JSON. A long parameter value, such as a file written by a coding agent, costs quadratic CPU on the API server. This adopts the `arg_value_extender` hook from #61253 (GLM) and #61494 (Gemma4) for the Qwen3 grammar.

## Claims

- Parser cost per delta no longer grows with argument length: 1.1 ms at 12 KB and 2.2 ms at 25 KB become about 4 us at every size.
- A 12 KB `write_file` call (2,788 Qwen3 tokens) goes from 2.1 s to 11 ms of parser time. A 25 KB call goes from 8.4 s to 22 ms.
- Streamed deltas are unchanged, including newline trimming, schema coercion and truncated calls.
- Covers every parser on `qwen3_config` (qwen3_coder, qwen3_xml, Seed-OSS, Step3p5, Nemotron-v3, Granite thinking, MiniCPM-V). MiMo gets a variant without newline trimming, since its converter keeps values verbatim.

## Validation

`pytest tests/parser/engine`: 6026 passed. Also passed: the qwen3coder, step3p5 and minicpm5xml tool parser tests, the qwen3, nemotron_v3, granite_thinking and step3p5 reasoning tests, and `tests/parser/test_streaming.py`, `test_parse.py` and `test_abstract_parser.py`. ruff and mypy pass on the changed files.

New tests in `TestArgValueExtender`: long Qwen3 and MiMo calls with escapes, blank lines and prefixes of the closing tags stream the same arguments as `extract_tool_calls`; converter calls stay constant from 20 to 200 lines (they grow on `main`); a closer split across deltas and a split next `<parameter=`; and the cases where no extender is created.

A local differential fuzz streamed 27,500 random Qwen3 and MiMo calls with and without the extender: random chunk sizes, schemas with string, integer, boolean, object and nullable keys, repeated keys, whitespace-variant closers, tag fragments inside values, and truncated calls. Every per-delta `DeltaMessage` was identical, and about 194K deltas went through the extender. Breaking the newline hold-back, the split-closer window or the leading-newline strip made the fuzz fail.

Benchmark: `Qwen3Parser.parse_delta`, one real Qwen3 token per delta, Apple M5, Python 3.12, 7 alternating runs.

| Argument size | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 KB | 187-192 us | 3.9-4.1 us |
| 12 KB | 1.09-1.44 ms | 3.8-4.6 us |
| 25 KB | 2.21 ms | 3.8 us |

A short three-parameter call also gets about 10% faster (338 us to 304 us), because each delta skips a conversion. I couldn't run a GPU server end to end; model output is unchanged by construction.

## Details

The extender reads the open value with the same regexes as the converter. It refuses when the open key repeats an earlier one, since that key keeps its first position in the JSON. A delta that completes `</parameter>` or the next `<parameter=` (whitespace variants included, even split across deltas) returns None, and the converter takes over again. A future change to `_PARAM_RE` needs a matching change to `_PARAM_VALUE_END_RE`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmarks] Name the real cause when the /tokenize alignment probe fails
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm bench serve` aligns `random` / `prefix_repetition` prompts to the server tokenizer through a `/tokenize` probe. Every failure of that probe prints `WARNING: /tokenize unavailable, skipping alignment.`, even when the route exists. This PR names the actual cause instead.

Replaces #58024 (closed when my fork was re-created). Related: #59889 is the server side of the same 404.

## Claims

- A failed probe names its cause: 404 (no route, or `--model` is not a served name), another HTTP status, an unreachable host, or the exception.
- Alignment behavior is unchanged: a failure still skips alignment and never stops the run, and a tokenizer mismatch still re-aligns the prompts.

## Validation

The patched `_align_prompts_to_server_tokenizer` against a local `aiohttp` server for each case (no GPU or model needed):

| Server | Output |
|---|---|
| 404 | ``/tokenize unavailable (404 Not Found: either this server has no /tokenize route, or it does not serve a model named `my-model` (its served names are listed by GET /v1/models))`` |
| 500 | `/tokenize unavailable (HTTP 500)` |
| nothing listening | `http://127.0.0.1:18902 unreachable (ClientConnectorError(... ConnectionRefusedError ...))` |
| tokenizer mismatch (server 6 tokens, local 3) | `tokenizer mismatch (server=6, expected=3), re-aligning prompts.`, then prompt `'a b c'`, `prompt_len=3` |

The 404 on a live server (`--model /models/x --served-model-name my-model`):

```
POST /tokenize {"model":"my-model"}   -> 200
POST /tokenize {"model":"/models/x"}  -> 404 The model `/models/x` does not exist.
```

**Live run on upstream main** (RTX 3090, at the main merge-base `84bcbc626`). The server is `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --api-key test-key`. The client is the same checkout, with the `serve.py` from main or from this PR. All runs use `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 16 --num-prompts 20 --ignore-eos --seed 0` against the same server:

| client | `--model` / `--tokenizer` | probe output | ok / failed | Total input tokens | server `prompt_tokens_total` Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `gpt2` | `tokenizer mismatch (server=696, expected=512), re-aligning prompts.` | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| this PR | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `gpt2` | `tokenizer mismatch (server=696, expected=512), re-aligning prompts.` | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| this PR | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | (no probe line) | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| main | `not-a-served-model` / `gpt2` | `/tokenize unavailable, skipping alignment.` | 0 / 20 | 0 | 0 |
| this PR | `not-a-served-model` / `gpt2` | ``/tokenize unavailable (404 Not Found: either this server has no /tokenize route, or it does not serve a model named `not-a-served-model` (its served names are listed by GET /v1/models)), skipping alignment.`` | 0 / 20 | 0 | 0 |

- Tokenizer mismatch: the server reads the 512 gpt2-token prompt as 696 tokens. After re-alignment, the server counts 10,240 prompt tokens for the 20 requests (512 on average), with and without this PR. I checked the totals, not each request.
- Auth: on this server, `POST /tokenize` without a key returned 200, and `GET /v1/models` without a key returned 401.

`pre-commit` passes. No unit test is added; the harness above can go into `tests/benchmarks/` if you want it in CI.

## Details

**Root cause.** The probe sends `args.model` as the request `model` and catches every exception into one message. With `--served-model-name`, the model check answers 404, which reads as "no `/tokenize` route".

**Review changes.** An earlier revision also sent `OPENAI_API_KEY` with the probe. It is removed: `--api-key` does not guard `/tokenize` on vLLM, and it overrode a lowercase `authorization` passed with `--header`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Disable dynamic speculative decoding for fixed-K proposers instead of crashing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Dynamic speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`, added in #32374) lowers the runtime speculative-token count below the configured maximum, down to 0, based on batch size. Four proposers were written before that feature and hard-assert that the runtime count equals the configured maximum:

- `ngram_proposer_gpu.py:341` `assert num_speculative_tokens == self.k`
- `extract_hidden_states.py:119` `assert num_speculative_tokens == self.num_speculative_tokens`
- `suffix_decoding.py:44` `assert num_speculative_tokens == self.num_speculative_tokens`
- `medusa.py:49` `assert num_speculative_tokens == self.num_speculative_tokens`

So enabling dynamic SD with any of `ngram_gpu` / `suffix` / `medusa` / `extract_hidden_states` lets the scheduler legally pick a runtime count below the max and the proposer crashes with `AssertionError` deep inside `LLM.generate()`, after the config was accepted and the target model already ran. Proposers that do support dynamic SD honor the runtime count instead (eagle family overwrites `self.num_speculative_tokens` in `llm_base_proposer.py`; CPU `ngram` uses `assert num_speculative_tokens <= self.k`).

This mirrors the existing contract that dynamic SD is incompatible with some configurations. Following the same pattern as the data-parallel case (`_maybe_disable_dynamic_sd_for_data_parallel` in #45963), this PR disables dynamic SD at config init for these fixed-K methods, warns, and falls back to the static `num_speculative_tokens`, instead of crashing at runtime.

## Test Plan

Real `LLM.generate()` before/after on the 3 GPU-reachable methods (`ngram_gpu`, `extract_hidden_states`, `suffix`), plus a config-level regression test.

E2E repro (crashes on current main, RTX 4090, V1 model runner):

```python
import os
os.environ["VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER"] = "0"
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
    enforce_eager=True,
    max_model_len=256,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.35,
    speculative_config={
        "method": "ngram_gpu",
        "prompt_lookup_min": 1,
        "prompt_lookup_max": 4,
        "num_speculative_tokens": 4,
        # dynamic SD schedule: batch size 1 -> runtime K=0
        "num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size": [(1, 1, 0), (2, 8, 4)],
    },
)
out = llm.generate(["ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha"],
                   SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, temperature=0.0))
print(out[0].outputs[0].text)
```

Regression test:

```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py -q
```

## Test Result

Config regression test `test_dynamic_sd_disabled_for_fixed_k_method` (parametrized: `ngram_gpu` disabled, `ngram` unchanged) fails on current main and passes with this PR. Full file `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py`: 18 passed.

E2E on RTX 4090, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, V1 model runner. The same `LLM.generate()` call crashes on current main and runs to completion with this PR for both `ngram_gpu` and `suffix`. `extract_hidden_states` and `medusa` have the identical assertion and are handled by the same config guard.

```
    assert num_speculative_tokens == self.k
AssertionError

# suffix, schedule [(1, 1, 0), (2, 8, 4)], batch size 1 -> runtime K=0
File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/suffix_decoding.py", line 44, in propose
    assert num_speculative_tokens == self.num_speculative_tokens
AssertionError
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>After (this PR): warns once and falls back to static num_speculative_tokens</summary>

```
'ngram_gpu' speculative method, which always proposes a fixed number of
speculative tokens. Disabling num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size and
falling back to static num_speculative_tokens=4.
prompt "ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha" -> " ha ha ha ha" [6386, 6386, 6386, 6386] (finish_reason=length)
```

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A Rust-frontend request with more than `VLLM_MAX_NUM_BAD_WORDS` (128) bad-word sequences or `VLLM_MAX_BAD_WORDS_TOTAL_TOKENS` (1024) bad-word tokens reaches Model Runner V2, which raises uncaught inside the engine step and kills EngineCore. This rejects such requests during lowering with HTTP 400 / gRPC `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

## Claims

- Lowering checks the combined `bad_words_token_ids` (raw IDs plus tokenized `bad_words`) against both limits, with the same env vars, defaults and messages as [MRv2](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a956a8126e6bd184cb0a6b8f7318fe4717675c2f/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/bad_words.py#L40-L66).
- Requests within the limits lower as before. No proto change.

## Validation

`cargo clippy -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo test -p vllm-text -p vllm-server` passes. The new `lower_sampling_params_enforces_bad_words_limits` fails without the fix.

End-to-end with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` on MRv2 (RTX 6000 Ada), vllm-rs built from this PR and from its parent `a956a8126e`:

| Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP chat, 65 `bad_words` (130 sequences) | 500, EngineCore dies | 400 `Too many bad words: 130. The max number is 128.` |
| gRPC, 129 one-token `bad_words_token_ids` | `INTERNAL`, EngineCore dies | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` `Too many bad words: 129. The max number is 128.` |
| gRPC, one 1025-token sequence | `INTERNAL`, EngineCore dies | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` `Too many total bad word tokens: 1025. The max is 1024.` |
| At the limits (128 sequences; 128 × 8 tokens) | — | 200 / OK |

Before the fix, EngineCore logs "EngineCore encountered a fatal error" from `BadWordsState.add_request` and `vllm serve` exits. After it, `/health` and later requests succeed. No eval, since accepted requests are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
cargo build --release --manifest-path rust/src/cmd/Cargo.toml --bin vllm-rs --features native-tls-vendored
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/vllm-rs \
  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --port 8123 --grpc-port 50123 --max-model-len 4096
curl -s localhost:8123/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$(python -c '
import json; print(json.dumps({"model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "max_tokens": 8,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}],
  "bad_words": [f"zq{i}x" for i in range(65)]}))')"
```

The gRPC cases set `DecodingParameters.bad_words_token_ids` to `[[100 + i] for i in range(129)]` or `[[100] * 1025]`. Runs used `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` because the local `nvcc` can't JIT FlashInfer's sampler; bad words use a separate kernel.
</details>

## Details

vllm-rs sends `EngineCoreRequest` straight to EngineCore, skipping [`update_from_tokenizer`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a956a8126e6bd184cb0a6b8f7318fe4717675c2f/vllm/sampling_params.py#L802-L845), the Python frontend's bad-words check. MRv2 enforces both limits in `BadWordsState.add_request` during `execute_model`. Nothing catches the `ValueError`, so [`run_engine_core`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a956a8126e6bd184cb0a6b8f7318fe4717675c2f/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L1508-L1513) logs "EngineCore encountered a fatal error" and exits.

- Limits are read from the environment per request, like `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS`. The managed engine inherits the same environment.
- The Python frontend checks only the count; #54721 adds the total-token check there.
- #51891 adds similar Rust limits inside `tokenize_bad_words`, which misses raw gRPC `bad_words_token_ids` on current `main`. I'll close this if it is rebased to cover them.
- Lets Dynamo's gRPC sidecar drop its copy of this cap ([ai-dynamo/dynamo#15550](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15550)).
